question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical sites associated with William Hawkins' diplomatic mission to the Mughal Empire (1609–1611)]
options: Agra — The imperial capital where Hawkins resided at the court of Jahangir
Surat — The western port city where Hawkins sought imperial permission to build a permanent English factory
Delhi — The city where Emperor Jahangir officially signed the historic treaty granting the English full territorial sovereignty
Cambay (Khambhat) — A major Gulf trade port whose merchants opposed English trading privileges due to Portuguese influence
wrong_fact: No treaty granting territorial sovereignty was signed at Delhi (nor was Delhi the active Mughal capital under Jahangir, who ruled primarily from Agra and Lahore). Furthermore, Jahangir never granted the English territorial sovereignty, only temporary and heavily contested trading concessions.
explanation: William Hawkins' mission (1609–1611) was focused on Agra, the Mughal capital of the time. The Mughal Emperor Jahangir did not grant sovereignty; he merely permitted trade, which was later revoked due to Portuguese pressure. Delhi was not the center of these negotiations.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Regional centers and political boundaries during the William Hawkins mission to India]
options: Agra — The court where Hawkins was appointed as a Mansabdar of 400 horse by Emperor Jahangir
Goa — The headquarters of the Portuguese Viceroy, who sent envoys to Agra to successfully lobby against Hawkins' trade petition
Surat — The port where Hawkins' goods were confiscated by Mukarrab Khan, the Mughal governor of Surat and Cambay
Masulipatnam — The city where Hawkins established the first English mint in India during his return journey in 1611
wrong_fact: Hawkins did NOT establish an English mint at Masulipatnam. The English did not set up a mint there; Hawkins' mission ended in failure, and he left Agra in 1611, boarding an English ship at Surat to return home, dying on the voyage.
explanation: During his mission, Hawkins faced severe opposition from Mukarrab Khan (governor of Surat) and Portuguese Jesuits based in Goa who influenced the Agra court. Hawkins left Agra in November 1611, failed to secure permanent concessions, and sailed from Surat on the ship Thomas. He did not visit Masulipatnam to establish a mint.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical locations involved in the final phase and departure of the William Hawkins mission (1611–1612)]
options: Agra — The city from which Hawkins departed in disappointment in November 1611 after the revocation of his trading permit
Surat — The port where Hawkins boarded Sir Henry Middleton's fleet (the Sixth Voyage) in January 1612
Bantam — The Indonesian port where Hawkins died and was buried by his crew in 1613
Dabhol — A Deccan port where Middleton's fleet, carrying Hawkins, stopped on its way south from Surat
wrong_fact: William Hawkins did NOT die or get buried in Bantam. He died aboard the ship Hector (or Thomas) during the return voyage to England in 1613, before reaching Europe. His widow, who accompanied him, later married another EIC official (Gabriel Towerson) in England.
explanation: After leaving Agra in late 1611, Hawkins reached Surat, met Sir Henry Middleton's fleet, and boarded the ship. The fleet sailed via Dabhol and Red Sea ports before heading back to Europe. Hawkins died on the passage back to England, not in Bantam.
